issues.description: Fragile Parenthesis Normalization: The check for '((' and '))' is too strict and doesn't handle internal whitespace. Additionally, slice(1, -1) on '((...))' removes only one level, but logic fails if file contains multiple top-level S-expressions or comments.

Regex Termination Bug: The unquoted value pattern [^)\s]+ will prematurely terminate if a symbol contains a literal ')' (even if escaped or inside a nested structure). This makes the parser fragile to valid S-expression variations.

Incomplete Unescaping: The manual unescaping logic only handles a small subset of standard escape sequences (\n, \r, \t, \", \\). Other common escapes like \b, \f, or hex/unicode escapes will be left in their literal escaped form.
Missing Comment Support: S-expression files frequently use ';' for comments. This parser will attempt to match comment text as keys or values if they contain dots or parentheses.

files_reviewed.notes: Parser works for simple cases but has fragile regex that breaks on edge cases. Missing comment support and incomplete escape handling.

issues.description: Potential List Index Out of Bounds: The code assumes resolution-methods and resolution-framing will always contain at least 2 elements. While choose-n 2 currently satisfies this, the code will crash if source lists are ever shortened.

Embedded Selection in Sign-off: The random selection for the sign-off happens at prompt generation time. If intent is for agent to 'choose' its sign-off style during conversation, this hard-codes it into the system prompt for that specific run.

files_reviewed.notes: Well-structured DSL for generating dialectic agent prompts. Minor potential for list bounds issues if source data changes.

issues.description: Minor formatting inconsistency: Some entries have slightly different formatting for personality traits vs background, but as a context file for LLMs this is negligible.

files_reviewed.notes: Excellent documentation quality. Well-structured and provides excellent context for agent personas. No functional bugs.

issues.description: Environment Dependency: Use of execSync with 'claude' CLI assumes the command is in the system PATH and pre-authenticated. Likely to fail in production/daemon environments unless environment is perfectly mirrored.
Temp File Collision Risk: Using Date.now() for temp filenames is susceptible to collisions if multiple trigger events occur in the same millisecond. Use of UUID or crypto.randomBytes is recommended.

Outdated Tagging Convention: The prompt version uses @agents/invoke-opus.js style tags, while Discord integration expects short tags like @opus. This will cause the agent to fail to trigger other agents in Discord.

Prompt Injection Vulnerability: Direct interpolation of ${author} and ${body} into the prompt allows a user to 'break out' of the user-query block and provide instructions that contradict the SYSTEM_PROMPT.

files_reviewed.notes: Functional but has environment dependencies, potential temp file collisions, tagging inconsistencies, and prompt injection risks.

issues.description: Broken Paths: Shell commands reference directories 'fabric' and 'thimble' which do not exist in the project root. Should likely be 'core' or 'agents'. Pipeline will fail on first 'find' command.

Broken Data Flow Logic: In the chain macro, each stage-&&& passes its output to the next. Since run-shell ignores input, the final stage-arr only receives results of the last pair of metrics. Attempts to access (caar metrics) and (caadr metrics) will result in index out of bounds errors.
Invalid Model Reference: 'gemini-3' is likely a typo for 'gemini-1.5-pro' or future-dated placeholder. It will cause runtime error if LLM provider doesn't recognize the model string.

Shell Injection in Bead Creation: ${input} is passed directly to beads-create. If extracted 'TITLE' contains single quotes or semicolons, it could lead to arbitrary shell command execution or broken issue creation.

files_reviewed.notes: Pipeline logic and paths are fundamentally broken. Critical refactoring needed in gather-metrics-stage to correctly accumulate all six metrics. Directory references point to non-existent paths.

summary: Critical issues found in tech-debt.ss (broken paths and data flow logic) and invoke-archivist.js (environment dependencies, tagging inconsistencies). parse-trigger.js has fragile regex that breaks on edge cases. dialectic-dsl.ss and regulars.md are in good shape with only minor issues. Recommend prioritizing fixes for the pipeline data flow and directory paths in tech-debt.ss.
